subject: Chemistry
title: Aqua Regia: The Royal Water
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Aqua Regia: The Royal Water.

hook.text: Gold resists almost every acid. But mix hydrochloric and nitric acid together and gold dissolves like sugar in water.

buildup.text: Aqua regia means 'royal water' in Latin—named because it dissolves the 'king of metals.'

discovery.text: Nitric acid oxidizes gold atoms. Chloride ions from HCl stabilize them in solution, preventing the reverse reaction.

twist.text: In 1940, George de Hevesy dissolved two Nobel Prize medals in aqua regia to hide them from the Nazis.

climax.text: After the war, he precipitated the gold back out of solution. The Nobel committee recast the medals from the same gold.

punchline.text: Two acids that dissolve gold. Nobel medals hidden in a jar of liquid.

quiz.question: Why did George de Hevesy dissolve Nobel medals in aqua regia?
options: To hide them from the Nazis by turning solid gold into a liquid solution
To prove that aqua regia could dissolve any metal
To create a new gold alloy for scientific use

details.summary: Aqua regia, meaning royal water, is a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids that dissolves gold and platinum, metals resistant to every individual acid..
details.whyItMatters: Aqua regia challenged the alchemical belief in gold's absolute perfection and indestructibility. It remains essential in gold refining, platinum processing, and analytical chemistry today.
takeaways: Neither acid alone can dissolve gold, but their combination succeeds
Nitric acid oxidizes gold while chloride ions stabilize the dissolved form
Nobel laureate von Laue's gold medals were dissolved in aqua regia to hide them from Nazis

faq.question: Why can aqua regia dissolve gold when neither acid alone can?
faq.answer: Nitric acid acts as the oxidizer, converting gold atoms to ions. Normally this reaction stalls because gold ions are unstable. But hydrochloric acid provides chloride ions that immediately bind gold ions into stable AuCl4 complexes, removing them from the reaction and driving it forward.

faq.question: How were Nobel Prize medals hidden from the Nazis using aqua regia?
faq.answer: When Nazi Germany invaded Denmark, chemist George de Hevesy dissolved the Nobel medals of Max von Laue and James Franck in aqua regia and placed the solution on a shelf. After the war, gold was precipitated from the solution and the Nobel Foundation recast the medals.
